title: Applying for the Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant
subtitle: What to prepare, how to find an eligible installer, and what to expect at each stage
excerpt: The Boiler Upgrade Scheme (BUS) provides a grant toward the installation cost of an air or ground source heat pump. The grant goes directly to the MCS-certified installer, who deducts it from your quoted price. This guide covers eligibility, installer selection, the application process, and common reasons for delay.
sourceNotes: gov.uk BUS guidance (updated April 2026) for eligibility criteria, grant values, and application process. Ofgem BUS voucher scheme administration guidance. MCS installer directory documentation.

glossaryTerms.definition: The UK certification scheme for renewable energy installers and products. MCS certification is required for BUS grant eligibility.
The UK government grant scheme providing money toward heat pump installation costs, administered by Ofgem.
A device that moves heat from outside air or ground into a building using a refrigeration cycle, achieving a COP of 2.5 to 4.5.

content.text: The
Boiler Upgrade Scheme
(BUS) provides a government grant toward the cost of an air or ground source
heat pump
. The grant is paid directly to the
MCS
-certified installer, who deducts it from your quoted price. You do not claim the grant yourself and do not receive the money. You pay only what remains after the grant has been applied.
Eligibility
The property must be in England or Wales. Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate schemes.
The heat pump must replace a fossil-fuel boiler (gas, oil, or LPG). Replacing an existing heat pump or electric heating does not qualify.
The property must have a valid EPC. If the EPC flags outstanding loft or cavity wall insulation work, complete it before applying.
No income test and no means test. The grant is available regardless of household income.
How the application works
Find an MCS-certified installer for heat pumps using the MCS installer directory (search by postcode at mcsregistered.com). Get at least two quotes.
The installer checks your EPC and confirms eligibility. They apply for the grant voucher through Ofgem's portal on your behalf before installation begins.
Ofgem issues a voucher to the installer. The voucher is valid for three months. If installation does not complete within three months, the installer can apply for an extension.
The installer completes the work and issues you an MCS certificate and a handover pack. They submit the claim to Ofgem, who pay the installer the grant value directly.
You pay the installer the agreed quoted price minus the grant value. Keep a copy of all documentation including the MCS certificate.
Common reasons for delay
EPC with outstanding insulation recommendations: get new insulation fitted and commission a new EPC before the installer applies. Budget 3 to 4 weeks for this.
Planning permission: permitted development covers most air source heat pumps. Conservation areas and listed buildings need planning consent.

Electrical supply upgrade: a heat pump on a single-phase supply may exceed the capacity of the existing service head. The DNO (Distribution Network Operator) must assess and approve; this can take 4 to 8 weeks.
Scotland and Northern Ireland

Home Energy Scotland (HES) provides an interest-free loan and a cashback grant toward heat pumps in Scotland. The Northern Ireland Sustainable Energy Programme (NISEP) has a separate structure. Contact the Utility Regulator (NIE) for current rates.
Troubleshooter

rows.symptom: Installer says you are not eligible but your EPC looks clean
rows.cause: The EPC may have outdated recommendations that are no longer feasible, or an error in the EPC
rows.fix: Commission a new EPC from an accredited energy assessor. A corrected EPC can make a property eligible within weeks.

rows.cause: Supply chain delays, planning permission delays, or contractor backlog
rows.fix: Ask the installer to apply for a voucher extension through Ofgem before the expiry date. Extensions of up to 3 months are normally granted with a written reason.
